fields.description_zh: 第1碼為 H者：表示為血液腫瘤個案其他第1碼非 H 者：詳見原發部位(CASITE)對照表血液腫瘤個案若要再細分 NHL(非何杰金氏淋巴瘤)、 HL(何杰金氏淋巴瘤)及 LEU(白血病)等血液腫瘤個案，在此欄位無法辨識，請用組織類型與性態碼 (HISTOLOG)區分。若是要分析各癌症部分(CASITE欄位)，也請先把NHL、HL、 LEU等血液腫瘤排除後再計算。
fields.description_en: If the 1st character is H, this indicates a hematologic malignancy case; for cases where the 1st character is not H, see the Primary Site (CASITE) coding table. To further subdivide hematologic malignancy cases into NHL (non-Hodgkin lymphoma), HL (Hodgkin lymphoma), and LEU (leukemia), this field cannot distinguish them - use the Histology Type and Behavior Code (HISTOLOG) instead. When analyzing by cancer site (CASITE field), first exclude NHL, HL, LEU, and other hematologic malignancy cases before calculating.

entries.label_en: From [year] the International Classification of Diseases in the NHI database was converted from ICD-9-CM to ICD-10-CM, so the comorbidity ICD-9-CM codes must be recoded to ICD-10-CM per the NHIA announcement. Uncertain correspondences are handled by the following rules: 1. Those with a comD10_DMC other code, and E10.21/E11.21, but without a comD11_CRF other code, are classified as comD10_DMC. 2. Those with a comD11_CRF other code but without a comD10_DMC other code are classified as comD11_CRF. 3-1. Those with both comD10_DMC and comD11_CRF other codes are classified by whichever other code was recorded earliest. 3-2. entries.label_en: Identity-category comparison table. Data before ROC 95 (2006) vs. ROC 95 and after: veterans/veteran-survivor household representatives — identity=4 before 95; identity=2 with insured-attribute=61 from 95 on. Insurance category '62' dependents — identity=5 before 95; identity=2 with insured-attribute=62 and unit insurance-category first digit 1/2/3 from 95 on. 3. Enrollment/disenrollment types: (1) Enroll: joins NHI upon meeting eligibility. (2) Disenroll: 1) death; 2) serving a sentence in prison/detention, or a security/reformatory measure, for 2+ months; 3) missing for 6 months (or from the disaster date if missing due to disaster); 4) becoming an active-duty officer, NCO, soldier, or military-academy funded student (changed to 'transfer out' on 2001-02-01); 5) loss of enrollment conditions (e.g. household moved out, residence permit expired, foreigner's work/study ended and left). (3) Transfer in: 1) change of insurer unit; 2) change of insured identity. (4) Transfer out: 1) change of insurer unit; 2) change of insured identity. (5) Cancel: NHIA cancels a doubly-enrolled insured person. (6) Interrupted transfer in: everyone eligible must enroll; if after enrolling a gap in enrollment arose (job change, identity change, address move, etc.) with unpaid premiums, and the person re-enters NHI. (7) Interrupted transfer out: similarly, a gap leading to exit from NHI. (8) Resume: 1) a missing person found within 6 months should cancel suspension and pay back premiums; if not found after 6 months, insurance is terminated retroactively from the suspension month and disenrollment processed; 2) a person abroad 6+ months resumes on the return date, but one abroad under 6 months cancels suspension and pays back premiums. (9) Suspend: 1) registered missing but under 6 months; 2) continuously detained 2+ months; 3) planned to be abroad 6+ months, except deep-sea fishing-vessel crew; 4) continued-coverage dependents (children, grandchildren) aged 20+ without earning capacity (e.g. disability-certificate holders) or still studying without employment. (10) Suspend-resume: the field changes to 'suspend-resume' when resuming after suspension.
